questions.q: According to the teachings on Christian living among non-Christians (Matthew 5:13), Jesus warned that if salt loses its taste, it is no longer good for anything except to be ____________.
options: thrown out and trampled under people's feet
fed to the swine in the fields
mixed with soil to help plants grow
questions.explain: Jesus emphasized that Christians must maintain their distinctive character in society: "But if salt has lost its taste, how shall its saltiness be restored? It is no longer good for anything except to be thrown out and trampled under people's feet."

questions.q: In teaching the principle of Christian giving (2 Corinthians 9:6), Paul uses an agricultural metaphor. He writes: "The point is this: whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows bountifully will also ________."
questions.explain: Paul assures believers that God honors generous giving by stating: "...whoever sows bountifully will also reap bountifully." This teaches that spiritual and practical generosity results in abundant blessing.

questions.q: In James 2:13, teaching about the necessity of showing love and mercy to all people equally, the apostle states a profound warning: "For judgment is without mercy to one who has shown no ________."
questions.explain: James 2:13 warns against a hard, unforgiving, or prejudiced heart: "For judgment is without mercy to one who has shown no mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment."
